slides.title: Familiarity Is the Biggest Risk
slides.content: In Year 1 everything felt new. In Year 2: You become comfortable. You assume things are fine. Habits become automatic. Hazards can stop standing out. Familiarity can lead to shortcuts and missed risks.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Familiarity Is the Biggest Risk'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Familiarity Is the Biggest Risk.

slides.title: Common Year 2 Slips
slides.content: Examples include: Not wearing lanyards consistently. Skipping familiar safety checks. Assuming someone else checked equipment. Ignoring things that would have been reported in Year 1. Taking shortcuts with risk assessments.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Common Year 2 Slips'? Select all that apply.
options: Ignoring things that would have been reported in Year 1
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Common Year 2 Slips.

slides.title: Refresh the Basics
slides.content: Even in Year 2 you must still remember: Fire exits. Assembly points. Reporting routes. PPE requirements. Safe working practices. The standards have not changed.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Refresh the Basics'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Refresh the Basics.

slides.title: Show Respect Still Matters
slides.content: The same expectations apply: Respect spaces. Respect equipment. Respect other people. Respect safety instructions. The difference is that Year 2 students have less excuse for not knowing these expectations.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Show Respect Still Matters'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Show Respect Still Matters.

slides.title: New Year 2 Responsibilities
slides.content: Depending on your pathway, this may include: Live media production. Broadcasting responsibilities. Editorial duties. Industry placements. Larger projects. More independent work. These activities bring additional professional responsibilities.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'New Year 2 Responsibilities'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on New Year 2 Responsibilities.

slides.title: Risk Assessments Still Matter
slides.content: A common mistake is saying: "We've filmed there before." This is not a valid reason to skip a risk assessment. Every location shoot still requires appropriate approval and planning.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'Risk Assessments Still Matter'?
options: It is only assessed in exams
A common mistake is saying: "We've filmed there before." This is not a valid reason to skip a risk assessment
It is optional and not required
It applies only to certain students
exercise.explanation: A common mistake is saying: "We've filmed there before." This is not a valid reason to skip a risk assessment

slides.title: Equipment Responsibility
slides.content: Year 2 students must: Return equipment correctly. Report faults. Store equipment properly. Avoid assuming someone else has done it. If you are the last user, responsibility is yours.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Equipment Responsibility'? Select all that apply.
options: Avoid assuming someone else has done it
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Equipment Responsibility.

slides.title: Speak Up Early
slides.content: The core message remains: Notice hazards. Notice unsafe behaviour. Notice uncomfortable situations. Tell someone early. Professional practice includes reporting concerns when necessary.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Speak Up Early'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Speak Up Early.

slides.title: Quick Revision Summary
slides.content: Key points to remember: Familiarity creates risk Avoid complacency Re-check your habits Complete risk assessments every time Take professional responsibility for safety Speak up early when something is not right. ,

exercise.prompt: Which of these points are in the quick revision summary? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: These points are summarised in the Quick Revision Summary.
